Historical investigation snapshot. The 173 candidates below were subsequently
fixed; see local-fix-report.txt for current results and performance.

Remaining CSS syntax mismatches: deeper investigation
Recorded 2026-11-01

Result

All 2,113 previously uncertain assertions received fresh native dependency
probes. Among the 2,236 saved mismatches, 178 are now confirmed blocks under the
current AST-only constraints, 173 have plausible local implementation routes,
and 1,885 remain unresolved. These counts describe assertions, not defects.
There was no fresh full WPT audit and no production change; the saved pass rate
remains 16,220 / 18,456 (87.88%).

55 additional confirmed blocks

48 distinct-source comparisons produce equal native Property values using the
native PartialEq implementation. These include color normalization/mixing,
grid line-name merging, unitless/range normalization and negative font-width
and font-stretch. Some serialization controls round floating-point components;
exact native components were used where needed, and equality was verified,
not inferred from similar output. All 48 chosen proofs use different source
strings. Together with the previous 121, this establishes 169 collisions.

The historical tab-size and text-decoration-thickness self-comparisons remain
invalid evidence. New comparisons of direct negative values against calc()
independently establish collisions. A blanket negative-result rejection would
also reject the valid ranged math spelling; native source-form provenance or
validation is needed to distinguish them.

Six valid slotted pseudo-element chains fail native parsing because
PseudoElement::valid_after_slotted has a fixed whitelist. Checkmark, picker-icon,
picker(select) and details-content are absent. Parcel rejects the chains before
returning an AST; an AST guard cannot add the missing acceptance.

One invalid :has(.a, 123) selector becomes :has(.a). The original and control
produce identical native stylesheet AST debug dumps, and Parcel source shows
forgiving list recovery with no discarded-branch marker. This proof uses debug
AST comparison plus source inspection, not Property PartialEq. The two previous
@scope recovery blocks remain unchanged.

These blocks apply to the inspected native parsing path and current constraints.
They do not establish permanent impossibility or rule out future native APIs.

173 local-fix candidates, in suggested investigation order

1. Reuse existing native value parsers: 10 assertions.

   Seven flex-basis cases (fit-content, min-content, max-content and stretch)
   become typed values through Lightning CSS's existing width/Size parser.
   FlexBasis itself uses the narrower LengthPercentageOrAuto representation.
   Reusing the existing preferred-size conversion may therefore be possible
   without adding CSS grammar or changing Lightning CSS.

   Three z-index numeric-math assertions succeed through the existing native
   number parser, while CSSInteger only expects a literal integer and has a
   calc TODO. Implementing a shared native-number route would still require
   correct CSS integer rounding, range handling and rejection of invalid literal
   fractions. The alternate probes demonstrate native parsing, not completed
   z-index integration or computed-value correctness.

2. Validate retained native selector components: 114 assertions.

   64 :has() cases retain empty/nested/forbidden components suitable for semantic
   review. 42 cases retain known functional pseudo-element names without their
   required arguments. Four retain bare functional pseudo-class names. Three
   use the nonfunctional view-transition pseudo-element as a function. One
   retains an invalid picker identifier.

   These are candidate AST guards, not 114 guaranteed safe fixes. In particular,
   recovery can erase distinctions and functional placement rules need checking
   against valid cases. Rerun the full selected syntax corpus after changes.
   Improving syntax acceptance/rejection does not implement feature rendering.

3. Review existing generated-content/counter conversion: 49 assertions.

   The syntax path currently accepts opaque Custom declarations that the
   existing engine converter already interprets using native token structures.
   Reuse may avoid a new parallel parser. However, the renderer converter also
   rejects valid custom counter styles, images and other unsupported content;
   its attr() strictness and reserved-name handling need review. This group is
   a review bucket, not proof that all 49 can be fixed by wiring in conversion.

1,885 unresolved assertions

  1,742 native property Unparsed cases after the ten alternate routes above
    133 remaining selector cases
      6 normalization candidates without a distinct-source equality proof
      4 layer-import fallback cases

The six normalization cases include negative Lab/Oklab lightness and legacy
color none/NaN behavior. Approximate serialization or NaN debug output is not
sufficient evidence of native equality. No new block was inferred from it.

Native Unparsed diagnosis buckets

Each assertion gets one priority bucket; these are neither distinct bugs nor
proof that all local routes are exhausted:

  380  native-color-interpolation-space-gap
  270  other-native-color-rejection
  191  native-linear-p3-space-gap
  170  native-color-layers-function-gap
  170  other-native-property-rejection
  130  native-subgrid-model-gap
  115  native-random-function-gap
   61  native-color-needs-currentcolor-context
   38  native-calc-size-function-gap
   36  native-clamp-none-boundary-gap
   36  native-contrast-color-function-gap
   36  native-modern-white-space-shorthand-gap
   34  native-anchor-function-gap
   28  native-dashed-function-gap
   27  native-tree-counting-function-gap
    8  native-calc-whitespace-before-comma-rejection
    6  native-inherit-function-gap
    6  native-non-finite-color-rejection

The largest source findings are missing color interpolation spaces (380),
missing display-p3-linear color-space support (191), color-layers (170),
subgrid representation (130) and random functions (115). Another 61 color cases
need currentColor/system-color context that native eager interpolation or
relative-color conversion cannot resolve at parse time. Generic tokens remain,
but using them is not permission to add a second CSS grammar.

Lightning CSS already supports relative colors, alpha(), light-dark() and
color-mix() in multiple spaces. It also already recognizes NaN and infinity
math constants. Neither entire relative colors nor all non-finite math should
be reported as unsupported. Missing spaces/functions and eager evaluation are
more precise diagnoses.

The native clamp parser lacks none-boundary parsing. Eight additional failures
involve whitespace/comments before commas: parse_sum consumes the whitespace
then errors on the comma. These remain unresolved, since a compliant native
route or normalization has not been established. No raw CSS string rewriting
or replacement math parser is proposed.

Other observed gaps include calc-size, anchor functions, tree-counting,
dashed functions, inherit(), and the modern white-space shorthand. An Unparsed
result alone is not enough to certify a dependency block: other native parsers
or existing AST consumers must still be investigated.

Evidence and validation

Exact assertions and evidence references are in css-syntax.jsonl. Fresh probe
outputs, chosen native equality proofs, alternate parser routes, selector
controls and package source anchors are retained alongside this report.
The existing Rust diagnostic was recompiled unchanged against the saved native
dependency bundle. No production or test code was added. Inspected Lightning
CSS and Parcel source files match their cached packaged crate archives.

Registry validation checks the unchanged 2,236 assertion identities, all prior
blocks, new proofs, candidate counts, evidence references, source/artifact
hashes, original WPT file/line locations and unchanged selection/expectation
ledgers. Rendering records remain byte-for-byte unchanged. A full WPT regression
run remains necessary when candidates are implemented.

Primary specification references used in investigation:
https://www.w3.org/TR/css-values-4/#calc-range
https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#relational
https://drafts.csswg.org/css-view-transitions-1/#pseudo-elements
https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/#color-mix
https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo-4/#tree-abiding
